text.p: The Kazak government has put forward a proposal to four banks to acquire Boeing 747s which would be part of a fleet renewal plan for Air Kazakstan, Yuri Lavrinenko, Minister for Transport and Communications, told Reuters here Monday. ....Speaking during the Annual Meeting of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, Lavrinenko said the government proposal was to launch a revamped airline company and talks were going on, first to lease two aircraft by October 1997, then to buy two further aircraft and then in 1998 to buy two more aircraft.

He said they realised this was an expensive route to follow. But they would continue to maintain and upgrade their Soviet aircraft. A good number were reasonably new and quite serviceable but others were very old and would have to be replaced.

The idea is to move to aircraft which fit in with international standards and we will progressively improve the fleet, he added. They were already changing the state's aviation institutions so that they were were up to international standards including from traffic control to airport management systems.

Lavrinenko said an increase is planned in the once-a-week train frequency to Beijing as it is considered an extremely important economic strategy for the rail network giving Almaty connections to Beijing as well as the Black Sea and Mediterranean for cargo. The rail system was working very well but they planned to purchase more locomotives and upgrade rail-telecoms and despatching facilities. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
